title: 2027 IEEE Symposium for Multidisciplinary Computational Intelligence Incubators (IEEE MCII)
summary: IEEE MCII provides special sessions in emerging and developing applied computational intelligence domains.

sections.heading: Symposium Chairs
bullets: Fenglei Fan, City University of Hong Kong

cards.title: Special Session in CI in Archeology
cards.text: CI for archaeology, cultural heritage, artifact modeling, reconstruction, and classification.

cards.title: Special Session for CI in Non-Traditional Computation Technologies
cards.text: CI across DNA, quantum, cognitive, affective, granular, and word-based computing.

cards.title: Special Session in CI in Aerospace Applications
cards.text: CI for aerospace missions, autonomous systems, spacecraft, UAVs, and situational awareness.

cards.title: Special Session in CI in Agricultural Sciences and Agroforestry
cards.text: CI for precision agriculture, agroforestry, sensing, climate adaptation, and farm management.

cards.title: Special Session in CI in Neuroscience
cards.text: CI for neurorehabilitation, BCIs, neural data, neuroimaging, and brain-inspired computing.

cards.title: Special Session in CI in Search-based Software Engineering
cards.text: CI and search-based methods for software testing, maintenance, design, and optimization.

cards.title: Special Session in CI in Maritime Technology
cards.text: CI for maritime systems, autonomous ships, underwater robotics, ocean data, and marine risk.

sections.heading: Scope
paragraphs: The integration of Computational Intelligence (CI) has become crucial in addressing complex problems that traditional approaches struggle to solve. To date, CI has found applications in diverse domains, including finance, healthcare and robotics, demonstrating its versatility and efficacy in solving real-world challenges. However, there is further potential in less explored areas of Applied CI where exploitation of the breadth of CI techniques can create new groundbreaking solutions in such domains or be applied to enhance other non-traditional technologies.

The symposium nurtures sub-fields of Applied CI, such as archaeology, agricultural sciences, aerospace engineering, neuroscience, and climate science, where there is strong potential for growth. The special sessions provide a venue for focused research in selected domains. Both theoretical and practical contributions are sought from industry and academia alike. All submissions to this symposium are directed to the individual Special Sessions or Workshops. There are no general symposium submissions.
